title: Sounding: Underwater and Deep Sea Sound Effects
shortText: 102 underwater SFX: four ladders (depth, sonar, breathing, hull) plus diving gear, a submarine and a wreck. WAV + OGG.
html:
A dive your game can take deeper

102 underwater sound effects built around four ladders: the water gets darker, the sonar contact closes, the diver breathes faster and the hull groans longer, one rung at a time. Wire depth, air, distance or pressure to a rung and the sound follows.

Licence, up front

Royalty free. Commercial use. No attribution required. Use it in as many games as you like, on any platform. The one thing you may not do is resell or redistribute the sounds themselves as a sound pack. The plain language terms ship as LICENSE.txt, with a copy and paste credit line for anyone who wants one. Everything is synthesised from code, so there is no upstream sample licence behind it.

Hear it first

There is a free demo on this page: 23 sounds copied unaltered from the paid files. All 5 depth beds, all 5 sonar loops and all 5 regulator loops, the shortest and the longest hull groan, a bubble burst with every take, a sonar contact, a hatch and the sunlit shallows loop.

Four ladders, one number each

A dive is paced: the light goes out of the water, the air runs low, something closes in, the hull starts to complain. Each ladder is a set of files named by rung (_t1 to _t5), so your game picks the rung from a number it already has.

  • Depth: 5 water beds for one dive, each darker and heavier than the last. Seamless loops; crossfade between rungs.
  • Sonar contact: 5 seamless loops of one ping and its return, from 25 to 71 pings a minute (one every 2.40 s down to 0.84 s) as the contact closes.
  • Regulator breathing: 5 seamless loops of a breath drawn through the regulator and an exhale bursting into bubbles, from 15 to 37 breaths a minute as the air runs low.
  • Hull stress: 5 groans of steel under pressure, longer at every rung as the dive goes deeper. Two takes each.

Checked from the shipped files, not promised: all 16 steps between rungs move the declared way (at least 8% in brightness on the depth ladder, 12% in length on the other three), and every ladder spans at least 1.5 times end to end. Failing steps: 0.

The dive around them

25 sounds for one dive, 72 files, every one with takes so the same bubble never plays twice in a row:

  • Diving gear: a few bubbles past the mask and a big exhale bursting into bubbles (each rising in pitch as it climbs), a gloved knock on a brass helmet, a stiff valve, an air tank against a ladder rung, the purge button.
  • Submarine: a hatch swung shut and dogged down, something striking the hull from outside, a seam giving way, a torpedo tube firing, the ballast blown, a depth charge going off above.
  • Sonar: one active ping into open water, and a ping with its return.
  • Wreck and seabed: sunken timber shifting in the current, an anchor chain dragged across the bottom, rock and coral tumbling, a porthole cracking, brass and coins spilling from a broken chest, something large passing in the dark.
  • Stingers and interface: a reveal (water drawn in, a heavy hit and a long groan of steel), a beating brass warning, and a quiet menu set.
  • 5 ambience loops: open water, the bottom of a trench, the engine through the hull, sunlit shallows with bubbles rising, and a wreck settling on the seabed.

Fit

  • WAV and OGG for every file, 16 bit, 44.1 kHz, mono, with a naming manifest listing every file.
  • 20 seamless loops with loop points in both formats, and none on a one shot.
  • 30 variation sets whose takes are separate renders, never one file re pitched.
  • One loudness band: the inner 80 percent of the pack sits inside 0.96 dB, so a depth charge and a menu tick share a mix.
  • Import notes for Unity, Unreal, Godot, GameMaker, RPG Maker and the web, and pack_proof.json with a sha256 and a measurement for every file: 947 checks, 0 failed.

Honest limits

These are synthesised, stylised sounds designed for games, not field recordings. The figures above are signal measurements, not a claim that anything sounds good; that is what the free demo is for. No sea creatures, no voices, no ships on the surface (those live in a separate pack) and nothing musical: a sonar ping is one struck tone, never a tune.

AI disclosure, stated truthfully: the code that generates these sounds was written with AI assistance. The sounds themselves are self contained procedural synthesis by Core Systems Asset Factory, with no generative audio model at any point. The cover art and store graphics are AI generated.

More from the same studio

  • Leeward, ships, sea and harbour: everything above the water this pack leaves out.
  • Wade, liquid, wet and submerged movement: the swim strokes and the wading.
  • Fathom, underwater maps for RPG Maker MZ: caustics, light shafts and kelp for the water this pack fills.
